findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple instances of hand washing, which ended by using bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted as the inspector modeled proper hand washing. Ensure hand washing occurs for at least 20 seconds, with soap, and warm running water. Hand washing should conclude with drying hands with a paper towel, and then using that same paper towel to turn off the faucet (to avoid recontaminating hands).
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to be dispensing 0 ppm Chlorine after multiple runs. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) primed the dish machine, replaced the sanitizer bucket, and removed a broken line. Afterwards the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Chlorine. Ensure the dish machine is primed and tested at a frequency to ensure the proper concentration of food contact surfaces- as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine).

[P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the tamarind and tomato sauces at the front counter cooler (identified as being Temperature Control for food Safety- (TCS) by the PIC based on ingredients and processes) to be above 41F (stem thermometer reading of 56F). CORRECTED- the items were moved from the working cooler this morning, and the facility will implement TIME AS A CONTROL until the cooler is serviced. Ensure items are used or discarded within FOUR hours until the cooler is observed to be cold holding food items at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

CORRECTED- the PIC placed dates on the foods and replaced old stickers that did not reflect the date of preparation. Ensure all TCS food items are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation counts as day one. Date marking must be dated based on the oldest prepared ingredient.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

Also, the diffusers (inner white pieces) of the soda nozzles had some buildup as well as the surface of the soda machine where the diffusers and nozzles attach. Clean and sanitize the nozzles, diffusers, and area where they attach as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup.
In equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Ceiling inside the microwave was soiled with dried on food splash. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Fish that was just cooked ~1hr prior to inspector arriving was observed on the cook line. Product was sitting in the wok but not being hot held. The internal temperature was 87F-97F. Food was for a delivery order that was to go out around 3pm. This is a bad practice to heat foods in advance and not hot hold them. Best practice is to make the food just prior to the delivery going out. Fish was to be reheated to 165F prior to delivery.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Tomato sauce and onion sauce in the bottom of the prep cooler had internal temperatures at 66F and 69F respectively. Sauces were out for ~20-30 minutes for preparation of sauces used to make food for a delivery order going out around 3pm. Sauces were removed from the cooler and the remainder of each were going to be used to finish the order. Any leftover portions after the order was prepared were to be discarded.

Cooked chicken that was held in the freezer and thawed in the walkin cooler starting around 9am this morning was observed with an internal temperature of 84F sitting out on the cook line. The chicken was removed from the  walkin cooler ~1hr prior. The chicken was for the delivery order going out around 3pm. Manager was advised to have the chicken cooked immediately and finish preparing the order or it would need to be discarded. Chicken was cooked for the order.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Plastic grocery sack was used for storage of raw chicken removed from the original packaging. Although the sack is a single service article it is not intended for food storage in direct contact with unpackaged or prepared foods. Use only food grade containers and bags, such as plastic food storage bags, for storage of unpackaged and prepared foods. 

Puddling condensation was in direct contact with cartons of whipping cream, a bag of cabbage, and a bag of peas in the bottom of the prep cooler. Products were removed to allow for cleaning. Provide a barrier between food and the bottom of the cooler to protect items from potential contamination caused by condensation entering packaging and/or causing damage after contact with packaging over time.
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 -3-306 of the FDA Food Code.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12 Plate used for storage of ice scoop was soiled with general buildup. Plate and scoop were taken to dish area for ware washing. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Ladles were observed in mint sauce and donut balls in the walkin cooler. Handles had fallen in product and were submerged. Utensils were removed from foods and taken to dish area for ware washing. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Case of food thermometer was soiled with buildup of grease. Ensure storage case is kept clean to protect stem of food thermometer from potential contamination during storage.
Cleaned equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.11 Stem of one food thermometer was burnt and had something hard stuck on the end of it. That thermometer was discarded. Facility had another food thermometer that was not damaged. 
Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, easily cleanable, and free of imperfections.
findings.citation_text:
4-201.11 & 4-202.16 Puddling condensation was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler. Get the cooler checked and any necessary repairs completed to eliminate puddling condensation.
Equipment shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. Nonfood contact surfaces shall be designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
A) dry storage shelves (dust); and
B) walkin cooler shelves (general buildup/food debris).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Both hot and cold water at the left automatic faucet in the women's room ran for less than 5 seconds when dispensed. Manager noted the faucet bought for replacement did not fit right. A new faucet had to be special ordered. Repairs should be done be the next inspection.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 - Grout was worn down along the floor to wall juncture in the dish area along the wall where the dirty dish drain board is located. Accumulation of moisture and debris was observed in the area. New floor tiles were said to have been ordered to complete the repairs.

Floor drain and cover were soiled with buildup of food debris by the back prep table adjacent to the handsink and ice machine. Clean the floor drain and cover. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. The whole process took less than 10 seconds, and the manual faucet was shut off without use of a barrier. CFM was advised of the issue and was asked to reiterate the importance of proper handwashing with all staff. An educational handout showing proper technique was provided to be translated to Punjabi for future reference. 
Employees shall use the following method to clean their hands: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply cleaning compound; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water;  and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Kitchen handsink in the back prep area was blocked by a laundry bag. Laundry bag was moved to allow for ease in access to the handsink. Proper use and accessibility of handsink was discussed.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the kitchen handsink in the back prep area. Handwashing sign was provided and posted during inspection. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Pans of various foods were uncovered on the cook line, in the walkin cooler, walkin freezer, and in the bottom of the prep cooler. Multiple foods in the walkin cooler were uncovered, and the shelving above was soiled with general buildup of food debris and dust. A few sections of shelving also had peeling paint 
Shelving in the bottom of the prep cooler was soiled with food splash over a pan of uncovered, cooked cauliflower.
Also, pans with butter and fresh, cut onions and green peppers were uncovered in an area on the cook line where the surfaces above and around the pans were soiled with splash and debris.
Proper storage was discussed. All pans of food were covered during the inspection.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11 Some mold buildup was starting to accumulate on the ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle. Cleaning frequency was discussed.
Also, the diffusers of the soda nozzles had some buildup.
In equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Ceiling inside the microwave was soiled with dried on food splash. 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Cooked and shredded potatoes were observed on a prep cart by the back door. Potatoes had surface temperatures of 55F-61F. Potatoes were cooked and cooled in the walkin cooler earlier today based on information provided. Potatoes were said to have been removed for additional prep within the half hour prior to inspector's arrival. Nobody was working with the potatoes at the time of observation. Potatoes were placed back in the walkin cooler until staff had time to finish preparation for dinner service. Temperature abuse was discussed; CFM was advised to limit time food is out of cold holding during prep. Also, place foods back in cold holding if prep is interrupted and will not immediately resume. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Prepared foods in the walkin cooler (spinach saag, lamb dish, and rice pudding) and in the server area cooler (chutney) were not labeled. All foods were prepared earlier this week. Foods were dated and kept for use. Educational handout on date marking was provided. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41ºF/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach available for use did not have proper labeling. Directions on the label had general cleaning and laundry instructions but no directions for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Owner purchased proper bleach during the inspection. Product label for approved bleach shows concentration of 150ppm; operator was advised to use test strips and verify proper concentration when solutions are prepared. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Two pans of tarka (onion and tomato) prepared earlier today were cooling in the bottom of the prep cooler. Pans were labeled with the time of 2:00 and temperatures of 120 and 140 on the pans. Internal temperatures were checked by inspector at 3p and observed at 127F-128F. Product had ~1hr to drop below 70F. Portions were split in half and placed in the walkin freezer to rapidly chill the product. Cooling methods were discussed, and educational handouts were provided. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Large serving spoon was observed submerged in a container of raita (yogurt based sauce) in the walkin cooler. Only a small portion of the top of the handle could be seen. Serving spoon was removed from the sauce.
Pitcher with greasy water was observed storing serving utensils on the cook line. CFM noted the spoons and storage pitcher are cleaned up to every 4hrs. Pitcher and utensils were removed for cleaning.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, may be stored in foods with the handles extended out or in a container. Utensils may be stored in water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container and utensils are at least every 24 hours or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Pan used for storage of clean utensils was soiled with food debris and splash. CFM noted the utensils are typically cleaned again prior to each use. CFM was advised to clean the storage pan daily/as needed to protect clean utensils fro potential contamination. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 Vegetable chopper was observed in storage area with food debris stuck in the grooves of the push block and on the cutting surface. Chopper was cleaned after the last use, but food debris remained. Precleaning and repeating the wash, rinse, sanitize process for heavily soiled equipment were discussed. Chopper was taken to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized again.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Both hot and cold water at the left automatic faucet in the women's room ran for less than 5 seconds when dispensed. CFM noted the faucet has to be replaced, and a new faucet will be purchased within the next week for installation by a professional plumber. The right faucet in the women's room works properly.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 - Grout was worn down along the floor to wall juncture in the dish area along the wall where the dirty dish drain board is located. Accumulation of moisture and debris was observed in the area. Repairs have been scheduled.
Electrical cover under the dirty dish drain board was broken. Replace the cover. 
Surface under the dirty dish drain board was soiled with grimy buildup. Clean the surface under the drain boards at the dish machine. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

6-5011.8 Kitchen handsink between the dish area and cook line was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin. Handles of both kitchen handsinks had varying amounts of debris accumulation. Clean the handsinks and all related fixtures. 
Plumbing fixtures such as handsinks shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Stem thermometers and cases were heavily soiled with buildup of food debris and grease. Thermometers and cases were set aside to be cleaned and sanitized. General maintenance of thermometers was discussed, and an educational handout on calibration was provided.

Soiled tongs were observed on the cook line hanging from the handle of the oven door. Tongs were from lunch time service. Tongs were placed in the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Use a bleach solution, designated for the thermometers, to wipe the stem before and after checking temperatures. Wash, rinse, and sanitize thermometer stems up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Maintain the storage cases clean.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Old labels were observed on containers of food in the walkin cooler. Make sure labels are removed and allow for proper cleaning and sanitizing of all surfaces. 

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
If labels or food debris remain after going through a ware washing cycle, then repeat the ware washing process as many times as necessary to ensure removal of all soil and debris, including a pre-soak and scrape process.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
(R) 750.830 - Sanitizer at dish machine was observed at 10ppm chlorine. The chemical bottle was changed, and the concentration was observed at 50ppm after ~5 cycles. Routine service was scheduled to occur around 12/22/17, but a call for service was made to Auto-Chlor prior to getting the sanitizer to dispense at proper concentration. Technician is scheduled to come in for service the morning of 12/21/17.

All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.
Use test strips to check the sanitizer concentration daily, and make sure it is maintained at 50-100ppm per the instructions on product label.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - General buildup of debris and/or grease and food debris was observed along crevices of equipment (between upper edges of coolers and prep table) and between ovens. 
Handles of coolers and other equipment were also soiled with buildup.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris. Make sure storage shelves in the dish area and lower shelves or tables are cleaned as needed to eliminate potential food sources for pests.
